description: What a disc image IS, by content (retail = the whole image is a known retail dump, launcher/discs/redump.json). The PAL image used for development is a MODIFIED image (no dump matches it); a tiny ISO 9660 image the judge writes with SLES_525.68 and the core file names is 'unknown but plausible'; one without the core files is refused; one whose SYSTEM.CNF boots the North American program is refused by the region-aware loader with its sentence; the launcher's card says the same in plain words.

user_disc.disc_line: [twinsanityevolved] disc: modified PAL image SLES-52568 (not the retail dump: 2,579,234,816 bytes vs 2,558,263,296; volume CRASH)
user_disc.region_line: [twinsanityevolved] region: PAL SLES-52568, the decompilation's own layout, 60 Hz (50 offered)
user_disc.why: the image is 2,579,234,816 bytes, the retail dump (Redump 4514, SLES-52568 v1.01) 2,558,263,296: the size alone is decisive, so the boot does not hash the image

user_disc_verified.line_starts: [twinsanityevolved] disc: modified PAL image SLES-52568 (not the retail dump: 2,579,234,816 bytes vs 2,558,263,296; volume CRASH); image crc32 bc22864a sha1 cf69ffd7ab5225ac5e8ffb6a494495743ba2b40a
user_disc_verified.why: --verify-disc hashes the whole image: the CRC-32 and SHA-1 of this file (measured independently with shasum -a 1 / zlib), neither a Redump one

manifest.identify_text: matches no known retail dump: 2,579,234,816 bytes vs 2,558,263,296 of Redump disc 4514 (SLES-52568 v1.01)
manifest.why: tools/discs/manifest.py compares the whole image with the table and refuses to label a file list retail unless the image is a known dump; no file is written

plausible.disc_line: [twinsanityevolved] disc: unknown but plausible PAL image SLES-52568 (its program is not a known retail executable; volume JUDGEPAL) -- This disc of Crash Twinsanity (SLES-52568, PAL) does not carry the original release's program (SLES_525.68): it may not play as expected.
plausible.why: a generated image: SYSTEM.CNF booting SLES_525.68, a made-up ELF of that name and the core files' names (byte patterns): the title's file set, but not the retail executable -- accepted with the warning

refused.disc_line: [twinsanityevolved] disc: refused PAL image SLES-52568 (missing: CRASH6/CRASH.BD, CRASH6/CRASH.BH, CRASH6/MUSIC.MB, ...; volume JUDGEBAD) -- It is a PlayStation 2 disc (SLES-52568), but not Crash Twinsanity: CRASH6/CRASH.BD, CRASH6/CRASH.BH, CRASH6/MUSIC.MB and CRASH6/MUSIC.MH are missing.
refused.why: a generated image with SYSTEM.CNF and the program only: not the title's file set

region_lines: [twinsanityevolved] region: NTSC-U SLUS-20909, through an address map (built in), 60 Hz (50 not offered)
[twinsanityevolved] region: the European program's file names over this disc's archive index: StartUp\Fonts\Crash -> StartUp\Fonts\Crash_Euro
ntsc_u.refusal_line: [twinsanityevolved] Crash Twinsanity: This disc's program (SLUS_209.09, sha256 894bbdca963ad021...) is not the one the port's address map for the North American disc was made from: another version or a modified program needs its own map (twinsanityevolved-modtool region-map --pal <the European disc> --disc <this disc>, put beside the game).
ntsc_u.why: a generated image whose SYSTEM.CNF boots a made-up SLUS_209.09 (with the core files): the region row is chosen by the disc's content, its built-in map is read (launcher/discs/region_map_SLUS-20909.json), but the map is keyed by the original program's sha256 -- the game stops before entering the game with the sentence a player reads
ntsc_u.before_wave3: exit 3 'needs an address map (region_map_SLUS-20909.json): none' -- the refusal of a release without a map (still the Japanese disc's: test_region_map)

setup_lines: A modified copy of the PAL disc: 20 MB larger than the original.
launcher.games_status: Ready to play. A modified copy of the PAL disc: 20 MB larger than the original.
launcher.why: the launcher's own screens test (engine/tests/app/launcher/test_launcher_screens.cpp, offscreen) with the real title and the development disc: the card appears with the quick identity while the image is hashed on the worker ('PAL · checking…'), then reads 'PAL · modified disc' with the sentence; the Games card says the same

ntsc_u_real.disc_line: [twinsanityevolved] disc: NTSC-U image SLUS-20909 v2.00 by size (the retail dump's 2,108,489,728 bytes; contents not verified: --verify-disc hashes the image; volume CRASH)
ntsc_u_real.verified_line_starts: [twinsanityevolved] disc: retail NTSC-U image SLUS-20909 v2.00 (Redump disc 13689; volume CRASH); image crc32 06c5bb4a sha1 4f1a56f633c1b500bf3e39a0df1fdc8f101018ff
ntsc_u_real.identify_text: RETAIL: matches Redump disc 13689 (SLUS-20909 v2.00): size, CRC-32 and SHA-1
ntsc_u_real.check_text: is the RETAIL file list -- every file matches

launcher.why: the launcher's models test (engine/tests/app/launcher/test_launcher_models.cpp realDiscIdentity, offscreen) with the real title's tables: the card says 'NTSC-U · checking…' while the image is hashed, then 'NTSC-U · original disc'

ntsc_u_real.why: the test set holds a retail NTSC-U v2.00 image (2,108,489,728 bytes, sha1 4f1a56f6... = Redump disc 13689, measured with shasum): the size names the dump at boot, --verify-disc proves it; tools/discs/manifest.py --label retail wrote launcher/discs/ntsc_u.json from it (the first file list of retail provenance: names, sizes, sha256s)

not_made: a one-byte-modified copy of the development image: the image is a modified image already (it matches no dump), and no file list of retail provenance exists to name a changed file against -- a copy would only repeat 'modified' at the cost of a 2.6 GB file
refrozen: 2026-10-25 (same day): the refusal names the mod tool's region-map sub-command (engine/app/host/region_map_make.h, written after this fixture was first frozen) with the Python tool as the alternative
refrozen_ntsc: 2026-10-26: the real NTSC-U case (6) added with a retail NTSC-U v2.00 image (--ntsc-iso; SKIPPED without it); the synthetic NTSC-U case (4) refrozen: the North American disc now has a built-in map, so a made-up program is refused by the map's executable hash (exit 4) instead of 'no map' (exit 3); the launcher plays the real disc (playable, no second badge).
